name: Leigh Syndrome with Leukodystrophy
aliases: Leigh Disease with White Matter Abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Leigh Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria with Leukodystrophy Features

criteria.description: Progressive neurological deterioration with psychomotor regression and hypotonia
MRI evidence of bilateral symmetric lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem with associated leukodystrophy
Elevated lactate levels in blood and/or cerebrospinal fluid
Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial or nuclear genes associated with Leigh syndrome
Necrotizing lesions with spongiform changes in brain tissue biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive neurological symptoms plus characteristic MRI findings and elevated lactate levels
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and guide prognosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral symmetric necrotizing lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem
pathognomonic.notes: Identified on MRI as hallmark of disease
searchTerms: symmetrical brain tissue death in movement centers
bilateral basal ganglia and brainstem damage
loss of motor skills in infancy
declining movement abilities early in life

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated lactate in cerebrospinal fluid and blood
searchTerms: raised lactate in spinal fluid and blood
high lactic acid in cerebrospinal fluid and bloodstream

common.symptomName: Oculomotor abnormalities including nystagmus and ophthalmoplegia
searchTerms: eye movement issues including shaking and paralysis

laboratory: Elevated lactate and pyruvate in blood and CSF
imaging: MRI showing bilateral symmetric lesions in basal ganglia, brainstem, and leukodystrophy pattern in cerebral white matter
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy with lactate peak
genetic: Mutations in mitochondrial DNA genes (e.g., MT-ATP6)
Nuclear gene mutations affecting mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes (e.g., SURF1, NDUFS4)

distinguishingFeatures: Later onset compared to Leigh syndrome
Mitochondrial myopathy with ragged red fibers

redFlags: Bilateral symmetric basal ganglia lesions on MRI
Elevated lactate in CSF and blood
references: Finsterer J. Leigh syndrome: clinical presentation and diagnosis. Pediatr Neurol. 2008.
Lake NJ, et al. Leigh syndrome: One disorder, more than 75 monogenic causes. Ann Neurol. 2016.
Orphanet Report Series: Leigh syndrome with leukodystrophy. Orphanet. 2023.
